title: Contradiction Resolution
summary: Teach the reviewer to reconcile conflicting cues before finalizing a finding.
learningObjectives: Recognize when later text contradicts an earlier interpretation.
Separate supporting evidence from weakening evidence.
Separate conflicting evidence from insufficient evidence.
Avoid freezing on the first plausible reading.
Re-evaluate the scene when new information appears.

definitions.contradiction: A later cue that weakens, reverses, or clarifies an earlier interpretation.
definitions.resolution: The process of choosing the most defensible interpretation after considering all cues.
definitions.contradictingEvidence: Evidence that pushes against a reading.
definitions.insufficientEvidence: A state where the available evidence does not support a stable conclusion.

reviewerPrinciples: Do not freeze on the first interpretation.
A contradiction lowers confidence even if the first cue looked strong.
Later context can overturn an earlier assumption.
Conflicting evidence may require review instead of a final finding.
Evidence must be weighed as a whole, not as isolated fragments.
Manual review is better than a premature finding.
reviewerQuestions: Does later text contradict the first reading?
Is the original interpretation still the strongest one?
Which evidence is supporting and which is contradicting?
Is the remaining evidence still sufficient?
Would another reviewer revise the first conclusion?

decisionTree.question: Does the contradiction change the interpretation?

examples.text:
يبدو أنه يوافق.
لكن لاحقًا يرفض الفكرة بوضوح.
يبدأ الحوار كاتهام ثم يتحول إلى تفسير.

counterExamples.text: Assume the first sentence is final even after later contradiction.
Treat missing support as if it were contradictory support.
counterExamples.reason: Insufficient evidence is not the same as conflict.

commonMistakes: Treating insufficient evidence as a confirmed contradiction.

questions.question: Is the first plausible reading always correct?
Can contradiction turn a finding into a review item?

gcamMapping.note: Use when later context weakens an apparent religious violation.
